primary_comparison: Development-selected memory versus development-selected strongest history baseline; NRMSE at b=3 on fresh confirmation records.

checks.group_aggregation: Mean primary NRMSE favors memory in all five task strata; two of ten individual checkpoints favor the baseline. Conditionwise reversals are reported.
checks.ecological_inference: Inference concerns average fixed-task intervention-response performance, not every agent or unrestricted environments.
checks.selection_bias: Five convenient preselected tasks and previously used released checkpoints; no population-representativeness claim.
checks.collider_conditioning: No agent excluded or selected on confirmation outcomes; both methods evaluated on the same complete fixed cases.
checks.base_rates: Schedules and noise levels have equal prespecified weight; this synthetic mixture is not a deployment prevalence estimate.
checks.regression_to_mean: Matched concurrent comparison; no selection of worst-performing confirmation agents.
checks.survivorship: All five planned development and ten confirmation runs completed and are retained.
checks.multiple_comparisons: One prespecified primary comparison. Budget, schedule and auxiliary-metric intervals are descriptive and not multiplicity-adjusted discoveries.
checks.analysis_flexibility: Protocol precedes execution; selection and source hashes locked before confirmation. Full candidate grid and unfavorable cases retained. This is a local protocol, not an external preregistration.
checks.causal_scope: Controlled physical intervention responses and method-component comparisons; does not establish general causal understanding or improved policy returns.
checks.temporal_direction: Tests confirm update-prefix causality and budget restriction. Future rounds, true maps, change labels, noise levels and test responses do not enter estimators.

interval_scope: 20,000 paired checkpoint-bootstrap draws, resampling two confirmation networks within each fixed task. Noise draws, rounds, queries and response coordinates are not independent networks. Development selection uncertainty and generalization to new tasks are not covered.
